text: Ray Stanford speaking. I'm at the office of the Defensor Chieftain in Saqqara, New Mexico.
I have just talked to a gentleman here who was on the site Saturday morning, some hours after the occurrence, while the imprints were still very clear.
And I want to ask him some questions. I wonder if he could tell us his name first.
Lewis Riddell. I'm the publisher of the L. Defensor Chieftain.
Regarding what was seen by you at the site, did you see the indentations or tracks while they were still very fresh?
Yeah, on the day of the rally it was the next morning, and that was Saturday morning,
and before hundreds of people had gotten a chance to obliterate all the tracks.
What was your impression of these tracks?
Do you think they were made by a heavy object or by a light object or by digging out or what?
I would say a heavy object coming down very slowly and made a full fire each depression
in a comparatively hard sand there in the draw.
And these were longer than they were wide?
About 12, I would guess, about 12 inches long and 3 or 4 inches wide.
And equally deep rafts landing to the center in a wedge, was that the description that was accurate on this that I've heard?
Well, probably a little deeper on the south side, I mean the north side of the way it landed.
From his description, the front of the plane, or the object, I'll put it that way, was facing south.
and the way it landed on uneven ground, there seems to be a heavy indention on the south side,
which indicates that more of the weight was there.
Yes, this would be logical to me because, as I recall from being there this morning,
the south side is downhill.
I mean, it kind of slants upwards to the north,
so there might actually be more weight on the south side if it were an object balancing,
sitting on these legs.
Was this your observation, too?
Yes.
Now, I hear there were two little indentations off to one side,
to the west side, sort of parallel with one of the lines made by two of the four legs.
Did you see these two indentations yourself?
Yes, I did.
There was someone in the crowd while I was on the floor.
One of them made a remark that it possibly footprints or if you want to describe it more
of a hoof print, but that wasn't the impression that I had of the thing.
And we decided in our story, in our newspaper, that we wouldn't go into that too deeply.
It sounded a little preposterous.
I see.
How close were these to the line formed by the two nearest footprints, we'll call them that, by the object's leg prints?
How close were they to the line made by the two nearest footprints?
Well, they were in a, practically in the center between the two indentions I made by the legs on the west side.
Yes.
And they were probably 36 inches, about a yard.
parallel with that line made by the two legs? No, they were, yes, parallel, I'm sorry. Yes.
Now, we won't speculate as to what these were. I was wondering, it was on the same side that
Zamora told me that he had seen some figures from a distance in white coveralls. Did he tell
Yes, they were on the same side, those indentions on the ground, the round holes, indentions
of them.
And talking to Dr. Heine, he implied that the lawyer told him nothing specific at all
about seeing any men, implied he hadn't even mentioned any men. He later seemed to come
down and say that he mentioned coveralls after very pointed questioning by one of the persons
to his presence, but did, in this talk with Zamora soon after the sighting, since you
were one of the first to be there, did he mention to you that he actually saw a man
or just coveralls?
He very definitely did.
He said there were two there.
Now, he didn't say anything about them being men, but you would not think so because he
He said that he, when he was still in the car, that one of them, both men or objects, had their back turned.
And one of them turned around and looked him square in the face.
That was his exact words.
And he very definitely said that he saw two men there at the object.
And he said immediately they disappeared and apparently got in the plane from the side, from the west side, and the plane lifted up and started off.
That's an interesting thing. It is known from the west side. This is pretty speculative, but if they got down the west side,
weren't there two circular indentations at the west side?
Yes, that's right.
Would you say these were in a position where, with speculation, we might think it could have been some stairs that had been folded down,
that had touched down there, that this looked like it could have been this?
Yeah, it's possible. I thought that later when I got to thinking about it.
You don't ordinarily think of men with quilts or anything like that, so I presume that,
but the remarkable part of it is that there was no other track set.
Yes, because I could think that if the men were small and childlike, as one report said,
did he tell you that, that they were childlike?
Well, that was his description telling us that they were small.
That's what he was...
I would think if they were that small, maybe overnight their footprints might have been destroyed by a little breeze or something.
Well, they could have.
The heavier ones would have remained a little more.
So it's only speculation that maybe these things were associated with a ladder of some sort.
or at least this might give us a reason why they were on the west side of the object,
since we know that, according to Zamora's report,
this is where the men disappeared into the object was on the west side.
Now, would you say that Zamora was still rather excited Saturday morning when you were there?
No.
No, he didn't get no of that part of it.
Zamora impressed me as a very calm and level-headed fellow,
not subject to a man's dispels or hallucinations.
impression of him and from the people's knowledge of him here in town where you say this seems to be
a general impression? Very definitely. Good. Well, I think that this will help me out in getting the
details of this case on record since I may not have time to talk to all of these things with
Mr. Zamora who's been bothered a lot by everyone questioning him and calling him on the telephone
and I certainly hear out.
